title: “spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene” — which prophets, and which words?
summary: Matthew 2:23 says that Jesus dwelt in Nazareth “that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene”. The verse does not name the prophets or the passage.
text: KJV Matthew 2:23: “that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene”. KJV Isaiah 11:1: “a Branch shall grow out of his roots”. KJV Judges 13:5: “the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb”.
reasoning: The verse gives a saying in quotation form and attributes it to “the prophets”, in the plural. A whole-word search of the packaged KJV from Genesis to Malachi finds no verse with the word “Nazarene”. The search finds “Nazarite”, a different word, at Numbers 6 (2, 13, 18–21), Judges 13:5 and 13:7 and Judges 16:17. The verse does not say which prophets are meant, which words are quoted, or how being called a Nazarene is the fulfilment of them. Possible readings, named only as readings: a play on the name of a place, with a prophetic word such as “Branch” at Isaiah 11:1; a connection with the Nazarite of Judges 13:5; a summary of several prophets’ statements about a despised person without one quoted verse. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the verses quoted. The word search is a word search of one packaged KJV text and does not examine the Hebrew or the Greek. The record does not say that any reading is the right one and does not claim that no other passage says more.

sides.label: A

title: “many bodies of the saints which slept arose” — who were they, and what became of them?
summary: Matthew 27:52–53 says that at the crucifixion “the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose”, and that after his resurrection they went into the holy city and “appeared unto many”. The verses do not say who they were or what became of them.
text: KJV Matthew 27:52: “the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose”. KJV Matthew 27:53: “And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many”. KJV Matthew 27:51: “the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom”.
reasoning: The verses report a mass rising of the dead and name no one among them, give no number beyond “many”, and say nothing of what followed after they “appeared unto many”: whether they died again, whether they ascended, or whether they were seen by anyone who recorded it. A whole-word search of the packaged KJV from Matthew to John finds “slept” at 13:25, 25:5, 27:52 and 28:13, and only 27:52 uses it of the dead; the phrase “the graves were opened” is printed only at 27:52. Possible readings, named only as readings: a physical rising of persons of the old covenant who then died again; a sign of the resurrection to come; a figurative description. The record does not decide between them.

title: “we have seen his star in the east” — what was the star?
summary: Matthew 2:2 has the wise men say “we have seen his star in the east”, and 2:9 has the star go before them “till it came and stood over where the young child was”. The verses do not say what the star was or how it did this.
text: KJV Matthew 2:2: “we have seen his star in the east”. KJV Matthew 2:7: “enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared”. KJV Matthew 2:9: “the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was”. KJV Numbers 24:17: “there shall come a Star out of Jacob”.
reasoning: The wise men call it “his star”, and 2:9 has it go before them and stand over a place. The passage does not say what kind of thing the star was, why only the wise men are said to have seen it, or how it could mark a single house. A whole-word search of the packaged KJV from Matthew to John finds “star” only at Matthew 2:2, 2:7, 2:9 and 2:10. Possible readings, named only as readings: a natural celestial event understood by the wise men; a miraculous light; a connection with the “Star out of Jacob” of Numbers 24:17. The record does not decide between them.
